bug_description.normalized: The staged 5-byte PoC drives fuzz_disasmnext into the TMS320C64x backend: byte 0 selects platform 27 (CS_ARCH_TMS320C64X) and bytes 1..4 form the single 32-bit instruction word 0x20202020. decodeInstruction_4 accepts that word and TMS320C64x_get_insn_id maps the resulting opcode to a public tms320c64x_insn value. TMS320C64x_insn_name then uses that enum as a direct array index after checking only id < TMS320C64X_INS_ENDING, but the vulnerable insn_name_maps array contains only three elements. For the reproduced instruction, id is at least 3, so return insn_name_maps[id].name; reads past the end of the global array and ASan reports a global-buffer-overflow READ of size 8. The fix replaces the truncated table with a complete enum-ordered name table.

source.description: First non-harness project statement that materializes the attacker-controlled instruction bytes into the 32-bit TMS320C64x word consumed by the backend decoder.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact 5-byte blob `55 20 20 20 20`. In `suite/fuzz/fuzz_disasm.c`, `0x55 % 29 == 27` selects `CS_ARCH_TMS320C64X`, and `cs_disasm` passes the remaining four `0x20` bytes here as `code[0..3]`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: Indexes the 3-element global `insn_name_maps` array with a valid TMS320C64x enum value `id >= 3`, reading the `name` pointer from outside the array. ASan reports the resulting global-buffer-overflow READ of size 8 at this line.

root_cause.description: The function checks only the enum sentinel `TMS320C64X_INS_ENDING` and never checks that `id < ARR_SIZE(insn_name_maps)`, even though the vulnerable `insn_name_maps` declaration contains only three contiguous array elements.

tainted_value_origin.code: size_t count = cs_disasm(handle, Data+1, Size-1, address, 0, &all_insn);
tainted_value_origin.note: After line 225 computes `i = 0x55 % 29 = 27`, this call forwards the remaining four PoC bytes as the TMS320C64x instruction buffer. Those bytes become `code[0..3]` at source step 1.

parser_admitted.description: This checkout compiles 29 platform entries because `CS_NEXT_VERSION` is 5 and item 28 (WASM) is present. The PoC's first byte `0x55` yields `27`, selecting `platforms[27] = { CS_ARCH_TMS320C64X, CS_MODE_BIG_ENDIAN }`; line 235 then dispatches bytes 1..4 into the TMS320C64x decoder, and the later crash at line 245 proves `cs_disasm` returned at least one instruction.

fine_trace.note: With `code_len == 4`, this packs the PoC bytes `20 20 20 20` into `insn = 0x20202020`, the exact 32-bit word handed to the generated TMS320C64x decoder tables.

fine_trace.code: result = decodeInstruction_4(DecoderTable32, MI, insn, address, info, 0);
fine_trace.note: Feeds `insn` into the backend decoder. The later execution of the `if (count)` block in `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` proves this call returned `MCDisassembler_Success`, populated `MI->Opcode`, and yielded one 4-byte instruction.

Maps the decoded internal opcode to the public `tms320c64x_insn` enum stored in `insn->id`. The later ASan crash at `insn_name_maps[id]` proves this id is a valid TMS320C64x enum below `TMS320C64X_INS_ENDING` but at least 3; any `id <= 2` would stay within the 3-element table.
Because `Size-1 == 4` and step 2 succeeded, `cs_disasm` returns exactly one instruction (`count == 1`), so the loop runs once at `j = 0` and passes `all_insn[0].id` into `cs_insn_name`.

This is the only bounds check before the table lookup. It compares `id` against the enum sentinel `TMS320C64X_INS_ENDING`, but the vulnerable `insn_name_maps` declaration at lines 1721-1726 contains only three contiguous array elements. There is no `id < ARR_SIZE(insn_name_maps)` check, and the `name_map.id` fields inside those elements do not create sparse array slots.

Indexes `insn_name_maps` directly with `id >= 3`, reading a `name` pointer beyond the 3-element global array. ASan reports `global-buffer-overflow READ of size 8` at this line, and the fault address lands in the global redzone between adjacent string-literal globals from the same translation unit.

format.contract: The exact 5-byte binary blob `55 20 20 20 20`. Byte 0 selects platform index 27 because `0x55 % 29 == 27` in this checkout, reaching `CS_ARCH_TMS320C64X`; bytes 1..4 are the sole big-endian instruction word consumed at `TMS320C64x_getInstruction`.
